messages:
incidents-bot: SEV2 alert — continuous-batch error rate spike on prefix/prompt cache. Autoscaling triggered, some tail latency > 5s. Paging oncall: @oncall-ml. Links: https://internal.ops/alerts/2145000123 :rotating_light:

oncall-ml: saw it. ramping into the dashboard now. RTT and token-per-second metrics look odd.

sre_ryan: any obvious deploys?

eng_ops_maya: deploy-bot shows a config change at 2144999000 — 'batch.window_ms' lowered from 50->10 and 'prefix_cache_hash_v2' rolled to 1% canary.

oncall-ml: that canary looks to have been accidentally ramped to 100% in the same window during an automated experiment. I see KV cache size jumping and lots of miss churn.

eng_ops_maya: oh no. that explains the spike. some hosts started thrashing on cache rebuilds.

prod_sam: customer impact — a few high-throughput tenants reported timeouts and slow streaming. CS queues getting pings. @cust_success_elaine can you surface any paying customers impacted?

cust_success_elaine: pinged top 5 accounts using dedicated capacity. two reported degraded generation and one opened a ticket (INC-9921). ETA for outreach 15m.

oncall-ml: mitigation proposal: 1) rollback the canary flag to previous (prefix_cache_hash_v2=0) 2) revert batch.window_ms to 50ms 3) clear prefix cache on the affected podset to force warm but controlled rebuild. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

infra_ben: +1 to rollback flags. clearing cache globally could cause thundering; prefer staged rollout: drain 10% pools, clear, verify.

eng_ops_maya: commands ready. recommend roll back config then scale down will help.

deploy-bot: Config change detected: revert prefix_cache_hash_v2 -> 0 by eng_ops_maya at 2145000701.

oncall-ml: rolling batch.window_ms revert now.

eng_ops_maya: running patch: ```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/serving-runtime BATCH_WINDOW_MS=50 --record
kubectl -n inference annotate pod -l pool=prefix-canary action=drain
for p in $(kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=prefix-canary -o name); do kubectl -n inference exec $p -- /opt/runtime/cli cache clear-prefixes --limit 1000; done
```

sre_ryan: logs showing repeated cache-evict errors during churn: ```
[2025-06-21T14:00:12Z] evict prefix key=abc123 err=tokenizer_mismatch
[2025-06-21T14:00:12Z] cache miss rebuild start key=abc123 len_before=0 len_after=0
[2025-06-21T14:00:12Z] rebuild failed: tokenizer.hash != stored.hash (v1 vs v2)
```

oncall-ml: tokenizer mismatch — the canary inadvertently switched to a new tokenizer hashing algorithm, so existing prefix keys became invalid but still consumed memory while failing validation, causing rapid insert/evict cycles.

prod_sam: important: which customer data touched? any PII?

oncall-ml: no customer plaintext exposed. keys are prompt-derived hashes; we only saw increased cache metadata. No logs show raw prompts.

cust_success_elaine: updated the affected customers — they'll be informed of a transient degradation; ticket INC-9921 marked as under mitigation.

infra_ben: after revert applied, CPU and mem on canary nodes dropping. latency tail reduced from ~6s -> ~800ms in last 4 minutes.

eng_ops_maya: still seeing a small bump in error rate for one pool. I'm going to cordon and redeploy one node to ensure cache directories are clean.

oncall-ml: go ahead, cordon/restart the podset.

eng_ops_maya: ```
kubectl -n inference cordon node/gpu-42
kubectl -n inference drain node/gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# wait for reattachment
```

deploy-bot: Rollout successful: BATCH_WINDOW_MS=50 at 2145000945 by eng_ops_maya.

sre_ryan: monitoring: token throughput normalized, KV miss rate back to baseline. I still see a handful of prefix rebuilds for keys that were created after the canary flip; they'll naturally warm.

prod_sam: customer impact summary for execs: affected window ~2144999000-2145000701 (~28m). ~3% of total requests had elevated latency, < 0.2% errors surface to clients. No data loss. Drafting a short blurb for customers.

cust_success_elaine: blurb ready, will send to impacted accounts and post incident note to status page after we confirm stability.

oncall-ml: post-mortem action items: 1) add guardrail to prevent auto-ramp of experimental tokenizer/hash flags 2) add validation to detect tokenizer/hash mismatches before canary rollout 3) add a rolling-cache-clear orchestration to avoid thundering 4) add synthetic prompt tests on canaries for 24h after any prefix or tokenizer change.

eng_ops_maya: logging the action items to INC-9921 and assigning owners.

infra_ben: FYI: I applied a temporary telemetry alert: if KV insert rate spikes > 5x baseline and tokenizer mismatch errors > 5/min, page oncall.

prod_sam: thanks team. please keep updates in this thread with final customer communication and postmortem link.

oncall-ml: monitoring for 30m quiet window then demobilize.

sre_ryan: acknowledged. I'll schedule a quick sync to walk through root cause tomorrow 10:00 PT. :calendar:

incidents-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Incident ID: INC-9921. Runbook: https://internal.ops/runbooks/prefix-cache-tokenizer-drift

eng_ops_maya: leaving follow-up note: remember to add a pre-deploy check to reject tokenizer/hash toggles unless a canary flag and ramp policy are explicitly provided.

cust_success_elaine: outreach complete to affected accounts. no escalations.

prod_sam: closing oncall for now. great coordination. :rocket:
